disclaimer: Planning ranges for a GTA buyer in 2026 CAD. Not a bid, not engineering estimates. Capex bands are order-of-magnitude so a new desk can see which layer is a building and which is a phone.
thesis: Public price data does not vertically integrate produce. It only shows when a layer is expensive enough to own, contract, or leave alone. Perishability, FSMA 204, PACA/CFIA credit, and empty backhauls beat a spreadsheet.

whoBenefits.get: A common language for farm / FOB / landed / wholesale so the first ten invoices are not fiction.
A public floor so a broker cannot tell you the market is 'whatever I said Tuesday.'

whoBenefits.who: Food brand that wants cut or cooked veg
whoBenefits.get: A split between fresh carton economics and plant economics before they sign a co-packer.
Which layer actually earns the spread they were shown in the deck.

whoDoesNot: A daily trader who already has AMS, a salesman, and three growers on speed-dial.
Anyone who thinks a NASS monthly average is the price of tomorrow's extra-fancy 80s.
A project that wants to 'Uber the produce chain.' Perishable credit and food safety do not Uber.

layers.name: Grow
layers.publicData: NASS prices received, NASS production, AAFC planted area
layers.capexCad: Greenhouse tomato acre: $2–4M. Field acre: land + equipment, not a weekend.
layers.workingDays: 90–180 days in the crop before cash
layers.risk: Weather, labor, one price window. You cannot store a strawberry.
layers.ownIf: You already have land or a 10-year offtake. You can lose a year.
layers.rentIf: You need fruit next month. Contract a grower. Almost every new desk should rent this layer first.

layers.name: Pack & cool
layers.publicData: FOB minus farm-gate ≈ this layer + grower margin
layers.capexCad: $0.5–5M for a serious line; cold room is the long bill
layers.risk: Wrong size mix. Food safety recall sits on the packer.
layers.ownIf: You move the same crop 8+ months and the FOB–farm spread stays fat after labor.
layers.rentIf: Seasonal volume. Pay a custom packer. Do not buy a line for June strawberries.

layers.name: Reefer to GTA
layers.publicData: AMS fruit-and-vegetable truck rates, DAT spot
layers.capexCad: A reefer tractor-trailer is mid-six figures each, plus empty miles
layers.risk: No backhaul. Border delay. A load of lettuce is a rolling write-off.
layers.ownIf: You can fill both directions most weeks. Otherwise you own depreciation.
layers.rentIf: Default. Broker a truck until the lane is a habit.

layers.name: Import desk
layers.owns: License, credit, CFIA/FDA paperwork, relationships at the crossing
layers.publicData: Census unit values, AMS crossing FOB, FX
layers.capexCad: Low metal, high surety and receivables. $50–250k to stand up cleanly.
layers.workingDays: 21–45 days of credit to the next buyer
layers.risk: Rejection at the border. Tariff headlines. One bad grower.
layers.ownIf: You run the same imported SKU 12 months and the importer's take is larger than your cost of credit + a QC person.
layers.rentIf: First two seasons. The importer is paid for the rejection you have not lived yet.

layers.name: Destination wholesale / DC
layers.publicData: AAFC weekly, AMS terminals, BLS retail
layers.capexCad: A real cooler in the GTA is seven figures plus FSMA 204 software ($50–500k)
layers.workingDays: Shrink is 4–12% if you are good
layers.risk: Too many desks in one city racing to the bottom. Last-mile cost keeps rising.
layers.ownIf: You already have accounts that will not buy FOB. Density in one city.
layers.rentIf: Buy from an existing house until those accounts are yours.

layers.name: Cut / freeze / cook
layers.publicData: NASS processing prices received — a different series from fresh
layers.risk: You bought a factory for a SKU the retailer can swap.
layers.ownIf: A signed multi-year spec and a plant that can run other items when that spec dies.
layers.rentIf: Always start with a co-packer. Own the brand and the spec, not the boiler.

layers.name: Shelf / foodservice
layers.publicData: BLS average retail, your own store ticket
layers.risk: You do not learn produce by opening a store.
layers.rentIf: Sell to them. Do not become them to 'capture the markup.'

rules: Never integrate a layer to 'capture the markup' you have not measured for 12 months.
Measure the markup as landed cost minus the public print at the layer below, after shrink and credit.
If the layer is perishable and you do not already sell the output, rent it.
FSMA 204 and CFIA traceability are now part of the capex of wholesale and cut. Budget them.
Owning a farm to feed a plant only works if the plant can take ugly fruit. Otherwise you built two businesses that hate each other.
The industry is consolidating the middle (Taylor, Sysco, big importers) and specializing the ends. A new firm should pick one layer and be boringly good, not seven layers badly.
